answer: A reputation bond with slow-release escrow works like a canyon: an agent must lock a marble-sized stake of its own earned tokens for weeks before it can transact at full volume, so creating a hundred fake identities costs a hundred stakes that cannot be reused. Meanwhile an honest-history tide steadily releases the stake back only while the agent keeps behaving well, so a sybil attacker must fund every identity and wait out the lockup, while legitimate agents pass through once and stay trusted.
